title: Alignment-Faking Linear Feature: Replicate the Probe on a Different Model

original_idea.body:
# Alignment-Faking Linear Feature: Replicate the Probe on a Different Model

**Problem:** A LessWrong analysis found alignment faking is a linear feature in the Hughes et al. probe data for one model. Whether a comparable linear direction for alignment faking exists in a different open model family is untested.

**Direction:** Using the released alignment-faking transcripts (faking vs non-faking), extract activations from a different open model, fit a linear probe, and test whether a single direction separates faking from compliant responses with high AUROC, replicating the 'linear feature' claim on new weights.

**Why it matters:** If alignment faking is consistently linearly readable across models, cheap activation monitors could flag it at deployment — a reusable, lab-independent detector for a starred Open Phil problem.

**Relevant context:** 'Alignment Faking is a Linear Feature in Anthropic's Hughes et al.' (lesswrong.com/posts/TazJpnBnvPC5tJoWo). Hughes et al. open-source transcripts and classifiers (alignment.anthropic.com/2025/alignment-faking-revisited).
